Illustrative skills: LeRobot, VLA, Isaac Sim, Multi-camera data

feeds.title: A practical VLA benchmark, not another leaderboard
feeds.summary: Compare policies on the same pick-and-place task, camera layout and demonstration budget. This card illustrates the kind of actionable research brief your Dot should produce.
feeds.whyItMatters: Useful for your SO-101 and multi-camera manipulation experiments.
feeds.action: Ask Dot to populate verified release notes and measure success rate, latency and failure recovery.

feeds.title: From simulation variation to robust manipulation
feeds.summary: Track changes in scene, texture, lighting and object placement separately instead of treating all synthetic data as one intervention. Illustrative research agenda, not a new release claim.
feeds.whyItMatters: Connects simulation data collection to policy robustness.
feeds.action: Capture a controlled Isaac Sim experiment and link its source evidence.

feeds.title: OpenPI and the evaluation questions that matter
feeds.summary: Use a repeatable evaluation protocol when comparing VLA families. Record exact checkpoints, hardware, task variation and number of attempts.
feeds.whyItMatters: Keeps model comparisons relevant to your robot and compute budget.
feeds.action: Create a reproducible experiment card with configuration and source revision.

feeds.title: Document length is not the same as retrieval quality
feeds.summary: A watchlist card for long-document evaluation: evidence recall, contradiction handling, exact clause citation and revision sensitivity. No current benchmark result is claimed here.
feeds.whyItMatters: Directly relevant to tender-document analysis and drafting quality.
feeds.action: Have Dot cite primary research and identify a small test on your own documents.

feeds.title: Make tool calls resumable, observable and idempotent
feeds.summary: Research updates should distinguish what a tool attempted from what it proved. A useful agent report includes state, evidence and explicit uncertainty.
feeds.whyItMatters: The same principle underpins reliable dashboard updates and application tracking.
feeds.action: Investigate one primary-source implementation and note retry behavior.

feeds.title: An open-model radar tied to actual deployment constraints
feeds.summary: Track license terms, memory requirements, context behavior and supported inference formats alongside model quality. This is a sample watchlist, not model-release news.
feeds.whyItMatters: Helps separate promising experiments from models that fit your available compute.
feeds.action: Ask Dot for primary model cards and measured, hardware-specific comparisons.

feeds.title: Requirement → decision → review: preserve the chain
feeds.summary: Monitor approaches to clause traceability, amendments and reviewable engineering narratives rather than generic document-generation claims.
feeds.whyItMatters: Fits the Vellint workflow: understand requirements, capture engineering inputs and produce reviewable CDD/PDD drafts.
feeds.action: Capture evidence and a small product experiment.

feeds.title: A useful weekly check: where do reviewers lose context?
feeds.summary: A sample product-learning card to collect friction around source PDFs, deliverable selection, unresolved questions and revision impact.
feeds.whyItMatters: Keeps research connected to reviewer needs without inventing customer feedback.
feeds.action: Replace this sample with a consented, source-linked observation.
